messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: service=canary-health-checks alert=canary-regression severity=P1
  details: spike in 5xx and p95 latency on canary fleet. see: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/dash/abc123
  triggered_by: canary-health-check (policy: deploy-canary-5xx-threshold)

oncall-eli: acked. I'm taking this. pulling logs + probe results now.

ashley: fyi deploy finished ~4m ago, image=redwood/serve:release-2026-03-15-rlhf-quant. Canary fraction 10%.

oncall-eli: seeing p95 go from ~1.1s -> 3.7s, error-rate from 0.2% -> 4.8% on /v1/embed (canary nodes only).

kevin: digging into canary pod logs, lots of repeated errors: `KVCache: missing entry for request id` and `RuntimeKernel: attention-kernel OOM? fallback path`
  example: `2026-03-15T02:12:34Z canary-1 serve ERROR request=abcd status=502 msg="KVCache miss + kernel fallback"`

maria-pm: any customer-facing errors? support ingestion shows a handful of 502s from one mid-market customer (acct: purple-inc). severity?

oncall-eli: preliminary: ~12 requests from purple-inc failed in the window, their user-facing requests returned 502. Not widespread but definitely customer impact for them.

oncall-eli: hypothesis: new quantized kernel path + canary workload pattern is tripping an edge-case in the kv-cache invalidator -> causes subsequent token decoding fallback that produces 502.

kevin: I can reproduce locally by running the new image with higher concurrency and a long-prefix workload. will instrument more logs.

ashley: suggestion: roll the canary back to previous revision (release-2026-03-14-stable) while we debug. can we do a quick rollback?

oncall-eli: +1. This is a canary fail with customer impact. We should rollback canary-only to avoid escalating to prod. Planning to run rollback now.

oncall-eli: Running rollback command (oncall in terminal):
```
kubectl -n canary rollout undo deployment/serve-canary --to-revision=12
kubectl -n canary wait --for=condition=available --timeout=120s deployment/serve-canary
```

ashley: starting rollback now. will post pod status.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: escalation to SRE Manager (kevin) because P1 not cleared in 5m.

kevin: on it. joining the channel. watching logs and telemetry.

ashley: pods terminating -> new pods up. rollout progress: 3/3 updated, 3/3 available. verifying traffic and error rates.

oncall-eli: error-rate on canary dropping back to baseline (0.3%). p95 trending down to ~1.2s. purple-inc errors stopped after rollback at 02:19 UTC.

ops-julian: taking over monitoring for the next 60m. I'll keep an eye on the customer and open a support bridge with purple-inc if any residual issues. @maria-pm can you own the customer comms?

maria-pm: yes, I'll coordinate with support. prepping a short note and will flag if they need follow-up.

oncall-eli: handing off to ops-julian. I'll stay available for debugging but stepping out for another rotation. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Update: Pager resolved - condition cleared. root_cause: suspected kv-cache + quant-kernel fallback regression in release-2026-03-15-rlhf-quant (canary). action_taken: rolled canary back to revision 12. follow-up: postmortem + test-case to repro kv-cache invalidation. owners: eng-runtime (kevin), eng-ml (ashley).

pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged -> resolved. escalation deactivated.

ops-julian: I created a short incident ticket: INC-2026-0345, assigned to eng-runtime. will attach traces & the reproducer.

kevin: I'll start a debug branch and push kernel-fallback guard checks. will include a regression test exercising long-prefix + concurrent decode.

maria-pm: customer comms drafted, sent to support for review. will share final with ops-julian.

ashley: log snippet copied to the ticket, including the `KVCache miss` stack and kernel fallback path.

oncall-eli: closing my oncall note. thanks all.

incident-bot: Thread closed (no active pages). Next steps: postmortem scheduled, regression test PR expected in <24h.
